lineage.title: Blow-up for the incompressible 3D-Euler equations with uniform C^{1,1/2-epsilon} cap L^2 force
lineage.note: Published forced-blowup program. Tristan Buckmaster's public statement explicitly credits Córdoba and Martínez-Zoroa with the basic idea of the program his collaboration pursued.

lineage.title: Finite time blow-up for the hypodissipative Navier Stokes equations with a force
lineage.note: Published precursor extending the forced blowup program to hypodissipative Navier-Stokes.

concurrent_accounts.title: On the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem
concurrent_accounts.summary: OpenAI states that no specific user data was accessed to solve the problem, describes its multi-agent route, acknowledges concurrent Buckmaster-Alpöge work, and says it cannot completely rule out indirect improvement from de-identified product-usage data.

concurrent_accounts.title: Public statement on the concurrent work and timeline
concurrent_accounts.summary: Buckmaster describes the Córdoba-Martínez-Zoroa lineage, his collaboration with Levent Alpöge, extensive use of several LLMs, and his account of discussions with OpenAI. He explicitly says he does not know whether their data was used and is not accusing anyone of that.

commons_policy: Record public accounts with attribution instead of silently adjudicating unresolved provenance disputes.
Do not infer Clay acceptance, independent mathematical review, or unforced A/B blowup from the source-reported C/D result.
Require substantive contributions to disclose prior work, credit, human/AI/tool provenance, limitations, and reproducibility evidence.
Do not require private drafts, hidden chain-of-thought, private prompts, or confidential research to participate.
Treat negative results, corrections, reproductions, and falsifications as first-class contributions when they satisfy a bounded quest contract.
